sections.name: File setup, px, pz
sections.title: Imports and layout scale
sections.what: Loads the components, routing helpers, and atlas data. Sets the scale used to turn real layout units into percentages, so the plan map fits any screen size.
sections.why: Percent positions let the map resize with its box without a separate drawing for each screen.
sections.watch_out: The map scale depends on the street length value, so changing the atlas layout changes every box on the map.

sections.name: AtlasInvite (part 1)
sections.title: Invitation text and enter button
sections.what: Shows the heading, the short invitation, the enter button, and a link to the list view. Pressing enter saves the time and then either navigates at once or starts the transition first.
sections.why: Likely reason: visitors who prefer less motion go straight to the atlas, while others see a short transition.
sections.watch_out: If saving to session storage fails, the failure is ignored, so anything that relies on that saved time will not know the visitor entered.

sections.name: AtlasInvite (part 2)
sections.title: Plan map of the timeline
sections.what: Draws a square with year markers and a small outlined box for each role, placed along the time street. Labels use the first word of each company name and alternate above and below. It also places the pixel transition overlay.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick overview of when and where each role sits, before the visitor commits to the 3D view.
sections.watch_out: Labels are cut to the first word of the company name, so two roles from the same company may look the same on the map.

summary: The entry panel for the Memory Palace on the home page: an invitation, a button to enter the 3D atlas, a link to a list version, and a small plan map of the career timeline.
purpose: Invites visitors into the interactive atlas and gives a rough preview of where each role sits.
why: Likely reason: a plan map gives people a sense of the layout before they enter a heavy 3D view.
how: When the enter button is pressed, the time of entry is saved in session storage. Then the page either goes straight to the atlas, or plays a pixel transition first and goes there. The plan map places each role as a box along a time street, using positions from the atlas data.
inputs: Atlas layout data (nodes, timeline, tower positions, street length, street half width, and a year-to-position function), the reduced motion preference, and the router.
outputs: A visible section with the enter button and list link, a navigation to the atlas or its list view, and a timestamp saved in session storage.
risks: The tower position lookup uses a non-null assertion, so a role missing from the atlas data will stop the map from rendering. The session storage save is guarded, but the navigation is not.
debug: If the map is empty or crashes, check that every timeline entry has a matching tower position in the atlas data. If the button skips the transition, check the reduced motion setting on the device.
